ourAnswer: Q = -26.9 MeV; fission not energetically possible (endothermic)
note: The printed key DROPS THE MINUS SIGN on its own result. Magnitude and verdict are both right; only the sign is missing. Read at 900 dpi to rule out a misread: there is a clear minus between the two mass terms and NONE before 26.90 — the '=' sits directly against it. THREE independent routes, and two of them are internal to the key itself, which is what makes this decisive rather than a difference of opinion: (1) the key's OWN printed expression, evaluated with the stem's OWN data (m(Fe-56) = 55.93494 u, m(Al-28) = 27.98191 u), gives 55.934939 - 2(27.98191) = -0.028881 u, x 931.5 = -26.90 MeV — so the expression the key prints contradicts the value it prints beside it; (2) the key's OWN verdict 'not possible' requires a NEGATIVE Q, since a Q of +26.90 MeV would be exothermic and therefore possible — the key would be refuting itself; (3) our independent derivation. The magnitude 26.90 is reproduced exactly, so this is a dropped sign in typesetting, not a computational error. Physically it is the expected result: Fe-56 sits at the peak of the binding-energy curve, so splitting it must COST energy.
